title: Input symbol at a configuration position
statement: Let $x$ be a bit string, let $q$ be an optional state from a four-state set, and let $i,m\in\mathbb N$, $h\in\mathbb Z$, and $o$ be a bit string. Suppose $i\le |x|$. In the configuration on input $x$ with state $q$, input head at position $i$, unary work tape content $1^m$, work head at $h$, and output $o$, the symbol under the input head is the bit at position $i$ when $i<|x|$, and is blank when $i=|x|$.
hypotheses_covered: $q$ is an optional state in a four-state set
replaced: Let $x$ be a bit string, $q$ an optional state in $\{0,1,2,3\}$, $i \le |x|$, $m \in \mathbb{N}$, $h \in \mathbb{Z}$ and $o$ an output word. In the configuration of a one-work-tape binary machine with states $\{0,1,2,3\}$ on input $x$ that is in state $q$, has its input head on input position $i$ (counting from $0$), its work tape holding $1^m$ in cells $0,\dots,m-1$, its work head at $h$ and output $o$, the scanned input symbol is $x_i$ if $i < |x|$ and the blank if $i = |x|$.
